question: How many minutes did the average US worker spend travelling to work, one way, in 2023?
source_title: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2023 1-Year Estimates, Table S0801 Commuting Characteristics
explainer: Round trip, that is nearly an hour a day - roughly 220 hours a year, or more than five full working weeks spent getting to and from work.

question: What was the average age of cars and light trucks on US roads in 2024?
source_title: Bureau of Transportation Statistics: Average Age of Automobiles and Trucks in Operation in the United States
explainer: US vehicles keep getting older: the average was about 9.6 years in 2002. Better build quality and high new-car prices keep old cars on the road longer.

question: How many keys are on a standard full-size US PC keyboard, including the number pad?
explainer: The US ANSI full-size layout has 104 keys: 26 letters, 10 digits, 12 function keys, the number pad, plus modifiers and navigation keys. The European ISO layout has 105.

question: How many minutes per day did the average American aged 15 and over spend watching TV in 2023?
source_title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics: American Time Use Survey - 2023 Results
explainer: About 2.6 hours a day, which is more than half of all leisure time. Socialising and communicating, by comparison, gets roughly 35 minutes a day.

question: How many litres of water does the average American family use at home per day, according to the EPA?
source_title: U.S. EPA WaterSense: How We Use Water
explainer: That is more than 300 US gallons, and roughly 70% of it is used indoors - toilets, showers and taps are the big three.

question: How many steps do runners climb in the Empire State Building Run-Up, from the lobby to the 86th-floor observatory?
explainer: That is about 18 steps per floor. The fastest runners climb all 86 floors in roughly 10 minutes.

question: How many yellow taxi medallions (licences to operate a cab) exist in New York City, as of 2024?
source_title: Wikipedia: Taxis of New York City
explainer: The number has been capped at 13,587 since 2014. At the 2014 peak a single medallion sold for over US$1 million; prices later collapsed to under $200,000.

question: How many different items does the average US supermarket carry, as of 2023?
source_title: FMI - The Food Industry Association: Supermarket Facts
explainer: The average store stocks almost 32,000 distinct products, yet a typical weekly shop touches only a few dozen of them.

question: How many post boxes does Royal Mail have across the UK?
explainer: Royal Mail aims to keep a post box within half a mile of 98% of addresses. Some boxes still in use date from the 1850s and carry Queen Victoria's cypher.

question: How many fire hydrants are there on the streets of New York City?
source_title: NYC Department of Environmental Protection: Fire Hydrants
explainer: That is roughly one hydrant every 100 metres along the city's 6,000-plus miles of streets, all fed by the water mains DEP maintains.

question: How many bridges are there in the United States, according to the National Bridge Inventory?
explainer: Almost half are more than 50 years old, and roughly 7% are rated in poor condition - yet they carry well over 100 million crossings a day.

question: How many vending machines are there in Japan, as of the end of 2023?
source_title: Japan Vending Machine Manufacturers Association: Number of Vending Machines
explainer: Roughly one machine for every 32 people - the highest density in the world. More than half of them sell drinks.

question: How many bricks were used to build the Empire State Building?
explainer: The 102-storey tower also used about 57,000 tonnes of steel and went up in just 410 days. Ten million bricks would build around 1,000 ordinary houses.

question: How many households were there in the United States in 2023?
source_title: U.S. Census Bureau: America's Families and Living Arrangements: 2023 (Table H1)
explainer: With about 335 million residents, that works out to roughly 2.5 people per household. Nearly 29% of households are one person living alone.

question: How many motor vehicles (cars, trucks and buses) were produced worldwide in 2023?
explainer: China built about 30 million of them, nearly a third of the total. Worldwide that is roughly 180 vehicles rolling off a production line every minute.

question: How many rides were taken on the New York City Subway in 2023?
source_title: MTA: Subway and bus ridership for 2023
explainer: About 3.2 million rides on an average day across 472 stations - still only around two-thirds of the 1.7 billion rides of 2019.

question: How many pieces of mail did the US Postal Service handle in fiscal year 2023?
source_title: USPS Postal Facts: Size and Scope
explainer: That is about 318 million pieces every day, delivered to roughly 167 million addresses - and still close to half of all the mail sent in the world.

question: How many litres of water does an Olympic-size swimming pool (50 m long, 25 m wide, 2 m deep) hold?
explainer: That is 2,500 cubic metres, or about 2,500 tonnes of water - enough to fill roughly 16,000 bathtubs or supply a US family's home for about six years.

question: How much did the average new vehicle sold in the US weigh in model year 2022?
source_title: U.S. EPA: The 2023 Automotive Trends Report - Highlights
explainer: A record 4,329 lb. The shift from sedans to SUVs and pickups has pushed the average up steadily since the early 1990s.
